name: XOUR
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ nonnegative integers. You can swap the elements at positions $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ if $$$a_i~\mathsf{XOR}~a_j \lt 4$$$, where $$$\mathsf{XOR}$$$ is the bitwise XOR operation . Find the lexicographically smallest array that can be made with any number of swaps. An array $$$x$$$ is lexicographically smaller than an array $$$y$$$ if in the first position where $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ differ, $$$x_i \lt y_i$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 2\cdot10^5$$$) — the length of the array. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_i$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the elements of the array. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output $$$n$$$ integers — the lexicographically smallest array that can be made with any number of swaps.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1971G — XOUR [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
